[Al-Abyad] said: "That I be with you, that I may learn your discipline, take from your works, and that we may unite in worship." He said: "I am occupied away from you." Then he turned to his prayer, and al-Abyad also turned to prayer. When Barsisa saw the intensity of his diligence and worship, he said to him: "What is your need?" [Al-Abyad] said: "That you permit me to come up to you." So [Barsisa] permitted him, and al-Abyad remained with him for a year, breaking his fast only one day in every forty days, and not turning from his prayer except once every forty days; and at times he extended it to eighty. When Barsisa saw his diligence, his own soul came to regard itself as lacking.

Then al-Abyad said: "I have supplications by which Allah heals the sick, the afflicted, and the insane," and he taught them to him.

Then he came to Iblis and said: "By Allah, I have ruined the man." Then he confronted a man and strangled him, and then said to his family—having appeared in the form of human beings—: "Your companion has madness. Shall I treat him?" They said: "Yes." He said: "I cannot prevail over his jinn, but take him to Barsisa, for with him is the Greatest Name of Allah, which if one asks by it, He gives, and if one calls upon Him by it, He answers." They came to him, and he invoked those supplications, and the devil departed from him.

Then al-Abyad began doing this with people, directing them to Barsisa, and they were cured.

Then he went to a girl, one of the daughters of kings, between three brothers, whose father had been a king; he died and appointed his brother [as successor]. Her paternal uncle was king over the Children of Israel, and he tormented her and strangled her.

Then [al-Abyad] came to them in the form of a physician to treat her and said: "Her devil is a rebellious jinn that cannot be overcome, but take her to Barsisa and leave her with him; when her devil comes, he will supplicate for her and she will be healed." They said: "He will not agree to this for us." He said: "Then build a hermitage beside his hermitage and place her in it, and say: 'She is a trust with you, so seek reward through her.'" They asked him this and he refused, so they built a hermitage and placed the girl in it. When [Barsisa] turned from his prayer, he saw the girl and her beauty, and he was struck with bewilderment. Then the devil came to her and strangled her; he turned from his prayer, supplicated for her, and the devil departed from her. Then he returned to his prayer, and the devil came to her and strangled her again.

He would uncover her and expose her to Barsisa. Then the devil came to him and said: "Woe to you! Have intercourse with her; you will not find the like of her, and you can repent afterward." He did not cease to urge him until he had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant and her pregnancy became apparent.

The devil said to him: "Woe to you! You have been exposed. Will you kill her and then repent, so that you will not be disgraced? If they come to you and ask you, say: 'Her devil came to her and took her away.'" So Barsisa killed her and buried her at night, but Satan took hold of the edge of her garment until it remained protruding from the dust, and Barsisa returned to his prayer.

Then Satan came in a dream to her brothers and said: "Barsisa did such-and-such to your sister; he killed her and buried her in such-and-such a mountain." They were appalled at this and said to Barsisa: "What became of our sister?" He said: "Her devil took her away." They believed him and departed.

Then Satan came to them again in a dream and said: "She is buried in such-and-such a place, and the edge of her garment is protruding from the dust." They went and found her, and they demolished his hermitage, brought him down, strangled him, and carried him to the king, and he confessed against himself, so [the king] ordered his execution.

When he was crucified, Satan said: "Do you know me?" He said: "No, by Allah." He said: "I am your companion who taught you the supplications. Did you not fear Allah? Were you not ashamed, though you are the most devout of the Children of Israel? Then your deed did not suffice you until you disgraced yourself, confessed against yourself, and exposed your likes among people. If you die in this state, none of your peers after you will prosper."

He said: "What shall I do?" He said: "Obey me in one matter, and I will save you from them and take their eyes away from you." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "You prostrate to me one prostration." He said: "I will do it," and he prostrated to him apart from Allah.

Then [Satan] said: "O Barsisa, this is what I wanted from you. The end of your affair is that you disbelieved in your Lord. Indeed, I am free of you; I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said:

There was a worshipper among the Children of Israel, one of the most devout people of his time. In his time there were three brothers who had a sister, who was a virgin, and they had no other sister. A military expedition came out [and went] against all three of them, and they did not know with whom to leave their sister, nor whom to trust with her, nor where to place her.

He said: Their opinion united upon leaving her with the worshipper of the Children of Israel, who was trusted in their own estimation. So they came to him and asked him to keep her, so that she would be in his care and protection until they returned from their campaign. He refused and sought refuge in Allah from them and from their sister.

He said: They did not cease with him until they persuaded him [or: until he obeyed them]. He said: "Lodge her in a house opposite my hermitage." So they lodged her in that house, then departed and left her. She remained in the protection of that worshipper for a time; he would lower food to her from his hermitage, place it at the door of the hermitage, then lock his door and ascend to his hermitage, and then he would command her, and she would come out of her house and take the food that had been placed for her.

He said: Satan dealt subtly with him, and continually encouraged him toward good, and magnified to him the girl's coming out of her house by day, and frightened him that someone might see her and fall in love with her.

He said: He remained in this state for a time. Then Iblis came to him, encouraged him toward good and reward, and said to him: "If you were to walk to her with her food until you placed it in her house, it would be greater for your reward." He said: He did not cease with him until he walked to her with her food and placed it in her house.

He said: He remained in that for a time. Then Iblis came to him, encouraged him toward good and urged him to it, and said: "If you were to speak with her and converse with her, so that she would be at ease with your talk, for she has become extremely lonely." He said: He did not cease with him until he talked with her for a time, looking down upon her from the top of his hermitage.

He said: Then after that Iblis came to him and said: "If you were to come down to her, sit at the door of your hermitage, and converse with her, while she sits at the door of her house and converses with you, it would be more companionable for her." He did not cease with him until he brought him down and seated him at the door of his hermitage, conversing with her, while the girl came out of her house, and they remained for a time talking together. Then Iblis came to him, encouraged him toward good and reward in what he did with her, and said: "If you went out of the door of your hermitage and sat near the door of her house, it would be more companionable for her." He did not cease with him until he did this.

He said: They remained for a time. Then Iblis came to him, encouraged him toward good and toward the goodly reward for what he did with her, and said to him: "If you drew close to the door of her house, talked with her, and she did not come out of her house..." So he did it.

He said: He would come down from his hermitage and sit at the door of her house and talk with her.

They remained in this for a while. Then Iblis came to him and said: "If you entered the house with her, talking with her, and did not leave her to show her face to anyone, it would be better for you." He did not cease with him until he entered the house, and he would talk with her all day; when evening came, he would ascend to his hermitage.

He said: Then Iblis came to him after that, and he did not cease adorning her for him until the worshipper struck her thigh and kissed her.

Iblis did not cease with him, making her beautiful in his eyes and enticing him, until he had intercourse with her and made her pregnant. She bore him a boy. Iblis came to him and said: "What do you think, if the brothers of this girl come and she has borne a child from you? What will you do? I am not sure you will not be exposed, or that they will not expose you! So go to her son, slaughter him, and bury him, for she will keep silent about you out of fear of her brothers, lest they discover what you did to her." He did so.

[Iblis] said to him: "Do you think she will conceal from her brothers what you did to her and that you killed her son? Take her, slaughter her, and bury her with her son."

He did not cease with him until he slaughtered her and cast her into the pit with her son, closed over them a great rock, leveled the earth over them, and ascended to his hermitage to worship there. He remained thus as long as Allah willed, until her brothers returned from the military campaign. They came to him and asked him about her. He announced her death to them, showed compassion for her, wept for them, and said: "She was the best of servants; this is her grave, so look at it."

Her brothers came to the grave, wept over her grave, showed compassion for her, and stayed at her grave for some days, then they departed to their families.

When night fell upon them and they took their beds, Satan came to them in the form of a traveling man. He began with the eldest of them and asked him about their sister. He told him what the worshipper had said, of her death and his compassion for her, and how he had shown them the place of her grave. Satan denied this and said: "He has not told you the truth about your sister's affair. He has made your sister pregnant and she bore a son from him; he slaughtered him and slaughtered her with him, out of fear of you, and cast her into a pit he dug behind the door of the house where she was, on the right of whoever enters it."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 16–17 (part 2 of 2):

"So set out and enter the house where she was, on the right of whoever enters it. For you will find them both there together, just as I have told you."
He said:
And he came to the middle one in his sleep and said to him the same thing.
Then he came to the youngest of them and said to him the same thing.
When the people awoke, they awoke astonished at what each of them had seen.
Some of them turned to others, each one saying:
"We have seen a marvel," and each told the others what he had seen.
The eldest of them said:
"This is a dream that is nothing, so let us go on and leave this alone."
The youngest of them said:
"I will not go on until I come to that place and look into it."
He said:
So they all set out until they entered the house where their sister was. They opened the door and searched the place that had been described to them in their dream, and they found their sister and her son slaughtered in the pit, just as they had been told. They asked the worshipper, and he confirmed the words of Iblis regarding what he had done to them both.
[[That is, they sought help from him against him, and he gave them justice against him.]] So their king sought redress against him, and he was brought down from his hermitage. They brought him forward to be crucified, and when they had set him upon the wood, Satan came to him and said:
"You know that I am your companion who tempted you regarding the woman, until you made her pregnant and slaughtered her and slaughtered her son. If you obey me today and disbelieve in God who created you, I will free you from what you are in."
He said:
So the worshipper disbelieved in God, and when he disbelieved, Satan left him between himself and his companions, and they crucified him.
He said:
Concerning him this verse was revealed: "Like the example of Satan when he says to man, 'Disbelieve.' But when he disbelieves, he says, 'Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'" ... to the words "...the recompense of the wrongdoers."
Ibn Abbas said: God struck this as an example for the hypocrites with the Jews. That is because God Most High commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to expel Banu al-Nadir from Madinah. The hypocrites secretly sent word to them: "Do not leave your homes; if they fight you, we will be with you, and if they expel you, we will be with you." So they fought the Prophet (ﷺ), and the hypocrites abandoned them and disowned them, just as Satan disowned Barsisa the worshipper. After that, the monks would only walk about with caution [[That is, they would show reconciliation and agreement while inwardly being otherwise.]] and concealment. The people of depravity and wickedness became bold toward the rabbis and accused them with slander and ugliness, until the case of Umm Jurayj the monk, whom God cleared. After that the monks were relieved and appeared openly to the people. It was also said: the meaning is that the example of the hypocrites in their treachery toward Banu al-Nadir is like the example of Iblis when he said to the disbelievers of Quraysh: "No one among the people can overcome you today, and indeed I am your protector" [al-Anfal: 48], the verse. Mujahid said: the word "man" here means all people, in the deception of Satan toward them. The meaning of His words, "when he says to man, 'Disbelieve'," is that he led him astray until he said, "Indeed, I am disbelieving." Satan's words, "Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds," are not literal; they are only a way of disowning the man, and so they confirm His words, "Indeed, I am free of you." Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read the yā' in "innī" with a fatha, while the rest read it with a sukun.
("So the end of both of them was") meaning: the end of Satan and that man ("that they are both in the Fire, abiding therein"). It is accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). The dual is clear for those who take the verse as specific to the monk and Satan. For those who take it in the sense of the category, the meaning is: "the end of the two groups or two kinds was..." The word "'aqibatahuma" is accusative as the predicate of "kana," and the subject is "annahuma fi al-nar." Al-Hasan read "fa-kana 'aqibatuhuma" with a raf' (nominative), the opposite of that. Al-A'mash read "khalidani fiha" with a raf', which contradicts the written form. He made it nominative as the predicate of "anna," and the adverbial phrase is cancelled.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾ regarding His commands and prohibitions, performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience.

(﴿And let a soul look to what it has sent forward for tomorrow﴾) means the Day of Resurrection. The Arabs use "tomorrow" (al-ghad) as a euphemism for the future. It was also said that He mentioned "tomorrow" to alert that the Hour is near, as the poet said:

"And indeed tomorrow is near for those who look."[[In Fara'id al-La'ali, it is mentioned that the speaker of this is Farrad ibn Ajda' to al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir. The verse's wording is:

"If the first part of this day has passed, then tomorrow is near to the one who looks at it."

[Surah al-Hashr (59): verse 20]

﴿Not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise, they are the triumphant.﴾]]

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He brought the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow. There is no doubt that everything that is coming is near, and death is certainly coming. The meaning of "what it has sent forward" is good or evil.

(﴿And fear Allah﴾) This is repeated for emphasis, like your saying: "Hurry, hurry!" and "Shoot, shoot!" It was also said that the first "taqwa" (fear of Allah) is repentance for the sins that have passed, and the second is guarding against disobedience in the future.

(﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾) Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: That is, with what will occur from you. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah﴾, meaning they abandoned His command.

﴿So He caused them to forget themselves﴾, meaning to do good deeds for themselves; this was said by Ibn Hibban. It was also said: they forgot the right of Allah, so He caused them to forget the right of their own souls; this was said by Sufyan. It was also said: they forgot Allah by abandoning His thanks and His glorification, and ﴿He caused them to forget themselves﴾ through punishment, so that some of them would not remember others; this was related by Ibn Isa. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: they forgot Allah at the time of sins, so He caused them to forget themselves at the time of repentance. The Exalted attributed the action to Himself in ﴿caused them to forget﴾ because it was due to His command and prohibition which they abandoned. It was also said: its meaning is that He found them abandoning His command and prohibition, as when you say: "I praised the man" (ahmadtu al-rajul), meaning I found him praiseworthy. It was also said: they forgot Allah in ease, so He caused them to forget themselves in hardships.

﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. Ibn Jubayr said: the disobedient. Ibn Zayd said: the liars. The root of fisq (defiant disobedience) is "going out" (al-khurud); that is, those who went out of obedience to Allah.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 59, verse 20:

﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the triumphant.﴾ (59:20)]]

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "He has brought the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow." There is no doubt that everything that is coming is near, and death is inevitably coming. The meaning of "what it has sent forward" is: what it has sent forward of good or evil.

(﴿And fear Allah﴾) He repeated this for emphasis, like your saying: "Hurry, hurry!" and "Shoot, shoot!" It was also said that the first fear of Allah means repentance (tawbah, turning back to God) for the sins of the past, and the second means guarding against sins in the future.

(﴿Indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾) Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "That is, of what will come from you." And Allah knows best.

[Surah al-Hashr (59): verse 19]

﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ (59:19)

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah﴾, that is, who abandoned His command, (﴿so He made them forget themselves﴾) so that they would not seek any good for themselves. This was said by Ibn Hibban. It was also said: they forgot the right of Allah, so He made them forget the right of their own selves. This was said by Sufyan. It was also said: they forgot Allah by abandoning His thanks and His glorification, so He made them forget themselves through the punishment, so that some of them would not remind others. This was related by Ibn 'Isa. Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: they forgot Allah at the time of sins, so He made them forget themselves at the time of repentance.

The Exalted attributed the act to Himself in ﹙﴿He made them forget﴾﹚ because it was due to His command and prohibition, which they had abandoned. It was also said: the meaning is that He found them abandoning His command and His prohibition, as in your saying: "I praised (ahmadtu) the man," when you find him praiseworthy. It was also said: they forgot Allah in ease, so He made them forget themselves in hardships.

(﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾) Ibn Jubayr said: "The disobedient." Ibn Zayd said: "The liars." The original meaning of fisq (defiant disobedience) is going out, that is, those who went out of obedience to Allah.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾, that is, in excellence and rank. (﴿The companions of Paradise are the triumphant﴾) that is, those brought near and honored. It was also said: those saved from the Fire. The discussion of the meaning of this verse has already passed in al-Ma'idah, at His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Say: not equal are the evil and the good﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 100] [See vol. 6, pp. 327.] and in Surah al-Sajdah, at His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal﴾ [al-Sajdah: 18] [See vol. 14, p. 105.] and in Surah Sad, ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on earth, or shall We make the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28] [See vol. 15, p. 101.] So there is no point in repetition. And praise be to Allah. [The phrase "and praise be to Allah" is missing from manuscript A.]

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on Surah 59, verse 21:**

21. His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split apart from the fear of God﴾. He urges reflection upon the admonitions of the Qur'an and shows that there is no excuse for neglecting contemplation (*tadabbur*). For if the mountains were addressed with this Qur'an, and reason were placed within them, they would yield to its admonitions. You would see them, despite their hardness and steadfastness, humbled and split (*mutasaddi'ah*), meaning cracked from the fear of God. *Al-khashi'* means the humble, and *al-mutasaddi'* means the cracked. It has been said: humbled before God by what He imposed upon them of obedience to Him, and split from fear of God lest they disobey Him and He punish them. It has also been said that this is by way of a parable for the disbelievers.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And these are the parables We present to the people﴾. That is, if We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, it would have humbled itself before its promise and split apart before its threat, while you, O people, who are overpowered by its inimitability, are not eager for its promise nor fearful of its threat. It has also been said that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ): meaning, had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, O Muhammad, it would not have endured, and it would have split from its descent upon it. We sent it down upon you and made you steadfast for it, so this is a favour upon him, that He made him steadfast for what the mountains cannot bear. It has also been said that the address is to the community (*ummah*), and that if God had sent this Qur'an down upon the mountains as a warning, they would have split from the fear of God. A human being has less strength and yet more steadfastness, so he upholds its right if he obeys, and is able to answer it back if he disobeys, since he is promised reward and restrained by punishment.

**Al-Qurtubi's commentary on Surah 59, verse 22:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Knower of the secret and the overt." It was also said: "He knows what has been and what will be." Sahl said: "Knowing of the Hereafter and of this world." It was said: "The unseen (al-ghayb) is what the servants have not known and have not witnessed, and the witnessed (al-shahada) is what they have known and witnessed."

﴿He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾. This has already been discussed.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He is Allah, other than Whom there is no god, the King, the Holy﴾. That is, the One free from every deficiency and pure from every defect. *Al-qadas* (with a vowel on the first letter) is the basin, in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, because one purifies oneself with it. From the same root is *al-qadus*, the singular of the vessels by which water is drawn from the well with the *saniya* [[From the meaning of *saniya*: the bucket and its equipment. What is meant here is the equipment by which the water is drawn.]]. Sibawayh used to say *qaddus* and *sabbuh*, with the first letter vowelled with a fatha. Abu Hatim related from Ya'qub that he heard a fluent Arab Bedouin, known as Abu al-Dinar, recite *al-qaddus* with a fatha on the qaf in the presence of al-Kisa'i. Tha'lab said: every noun on the pattern *fa'ul* has a fatha on its first letter, such as *safud* [[*Safud*: an iron skewer on which meat is roasted; its plural is *safafid*. *Kalub*: an iron hook bent like a hook for a ferry. *Tannur*: a clay oven in which bread is baked. *Samur*: a wild animal resembling a cat, whose skin is used to make valuable furs for their softness, lightness, warmth and beauty. *Shabut*: a fish with a thin tail, broad middle, smooth to the touch and small head. Its plural is *shababit*.]] and *kalub*, *tannur*, *samur* and *shabut*. The exceptions are *subbuh* and *quddus*, for in these the damma is more common, though they may also be read with a fatha. Likewise *dhurruh* [[*Dhurruh*: a small red creeping insect speckled with black, which flies, and is among the deadly poisons.]] is with a damma, and it may also be read with a fatha.

﴿Al-Salam﴾, that is, the One possessing freedom from all imperfections. Ibn al-'Arabi said: The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, agreed that the meaning of our saying about Allah, *al-Salam*, is an attribution (*nisba*), its implied meaning being "the One possessing safety." They then differed about how to render this attribution into three views. The first: its meaning is the One who is free from every defect and clear of every deficiency. The second: its meaning is "the One who grants peace," that is, the One who greets His servants in Paradise, as He said: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58]. The third: that its meaning is the One from whose injustice the creation is safe. I say: this is the view of al-Khattabi, and according to it, and according to the one before it, it is an attribute of action (*sifat fi'l*). But if it means the One free from defects and deficiencies, it is an essential attribute (*sifat dhat*). It has also been said: *al-Salam* means "the One who grants peace to His servants."

﴿Al-Mu'min﴾, that is, the One who confirms His messengers by manifesting His miracles through them, and who confirms for the believers what He promised them of reward, and confirms for the disbelievers what He threatened them with of punishment. It has also been said: *al-Mu'min* is the One who grants security to His friends from His punishment and grants security to His servants from His injustice. It is said: *amanahu* from *al-aman*, which is the opposite of fear, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿and He made them safe from fear﴾ [Quraysh: 4]; so He is *Mu'min*. Al-Nabigha said:

*And the Granter of security to the birds that seek refuge (in the Sacred House), whom the riders of Makkah wipe, between the thicket and the mountain slope.* [[*Al-'a'idhat*: what has taken refuge in the House from birds. *Al-ghil*: a dense, interwoven thicket. *Al-sanad*: what faces you of the mountain and rises above its foot.]]

Mujahid said: *al-Mu'min* is the One who declared His own unity by saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. Ibn 'Abbas said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people of monotheism will be brought out of the Fire. The first to come out will be those whose names match the name of a prophet. When no one remains in it whose name matches the name of a prophet, Allah the Exalted will say to those who remain: "You are the Muslims and I am *al-Salam*; you are the believers and I am *al-Mu'min*," and He will bring them out of the Fire by the blessing of these two names.

﴿Al-Muhaymin al-'Aziz﴾. The discussion of *al-Muhaymin* has preceded in *al-Ma'idah* [[See vol. 6, p. 210.]], and of *al-'Aziz* in other places [[See vol. 2, p. 131.]]. ﴿Al-Jabbar﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He is the Great. The *jabarut* of Allah is His greatness. On this view it is an essential attribute, from their saying: *nakhla jabbara* (a towering palm). Imru' al-Qays said:

*Tall palms, with dense branches, and high clusters of red unripe dates (al-busr), beyond the reach of the hand.* [[*Sawamiq*: tall. *Athith*: dense, intertwined. *Qinwan*: a cluster of dates.]]

He means the palm that is beyond reach of the hand. So this name indicates the greatness of Allah and His holiness above being touched by deficiencies and the attributes of createdness. It has also been said: it is from *al-jabr*, which is mending: one says *jabartu al-'azm fa-jabar* when one sets a bone after it has broken, so it is *fa'\"al* from *jabara*, meaning he mended the broken and enriched the poor. Al-Farra' said: it is from *ajbarahu 'ala al-amr*, meaning he compelled him to it. He said: I have not heard a *fa''al* form derived from *af'ala* except in *jabbar* and *darrak* from *adraka*. It has also been said: *al-Jabbar* is the One whose might cannot be withstood.

﴿Al-Mutakabbir﴾, the One who is greatly exalted in His lordship, so there is nothing like Him. It has also been said: *al-Mutakabbir* is the One exalted above every evil, the One who is too great for attributes of createdness and blame. The root of *al-kibr* and *al-kibriya'* is refusal and unwillingness to submit. Hamid ibn Thawr said:

*It was effaced as a weaned calf effaces (its traces), and the pride of the stubborn one has become, in it, obedient.*

The *kibriya'* is praise in the attributes of Allah, but blame in the attributes of created beings. In the authentic report from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, that He said: "Greatness is My cloak and majesty is My garment; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will break him, then cast him into the Fire." It has also been said: *al-Mutakabbir* means *al-'Ali* (the Most High). It has also been said: its meaning is *al-Kabir* (the Great), because He is too exalted to affect pride. It may be said: *tazallama* with the meaning of *zalama*, *tashattama* with the meaning of *shatama*, and *istaqarra* with the meaning of *qarra*. Likewise *al-Mutakabbir* means *al-Kabir*. It is not as when the created being is described with it, when it is described with the form *tafa''ala* in reference to what did not belong to him. Then He declared Himself free of what they associate: ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾, that is, a declaration of His transcendence for His majesty and greatness, above what they associate with Him.

**Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 59, verse 24:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾. Here *al-Khaliq* (the Creator) means *al-Muqaddir* (the One who measures and decrees). *Al-Bari'* (the Originator) means *al-Mun'shi'* (the One who brings into being) and *al-Mukhtari'* (the One who innovates). *Al-Musawwir* (the Fashioner) is the one who gives forms to things and composes them into different shapes. Thus fashioning (*al-taswir*) follows creation (*al-khalq*) and origination (*al-bara'ah*) and comes after both of them. The meaning of *al-taswir* is drawing the outline and shaping. Allah created the human being in the wombs of mothers in three creations: He made him a clinging clot (*'alaqah*), then a lump of flesh (*mudghah*), then He gave him a form (*surah*), which is the shaping by which he becomes a figure and a configuration, recognised by it and distinguished from others by its marks. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.

Al-Nabighah said:

*The Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, who in the wombs*
*(shapes him) from water until he becomes blood.*

Some people have made *al-khalq* mean *al-taswir*, but this is not so. Rather, *al-taswir* comes last, *al-taqdir* (measuring) comes first, and *al-bara'ah* (origination) lies between them. From this is the saying of the Truth (Allah): ﴿And when you shape from clay like the form of a bird﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 110]. [See vol. 6, p. 362.]

Zuhayr said:

*You measure what you have created, while some of the people create but do not measure (it out).*

He means: you decide what you will decree, then you carry it out (*tafri-hi*), that is, you make it happen according to your decree. Another person decrees what cannot be completed for him and in which his aim does not come to pass, either because of his deficiency in conceiving his decree or because of his inability to achieve his aim in full.

We have dealt with all of this in *al-Kitab al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna* (The Most Excellent Book on Explaining the Beautiful Names of Allah), and praise be to Allah.

It is narrated from Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah that he recited *al-Bari'u al-Musawwara* with a fatha on the *waw* and a fatha on the *ra'*, meaning: the One who originates the fashioned thing (*al-musawwar*), that is, who distinguishes what He fashions by the variation of forms. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this.

﴿To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾. The discussion of this has already passed. [See vol. 1, p. 287; vol. 2, p. 131; and vol. 10, p. 266.]

It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: I asked my close friend, Abu al-Qasim, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), about the Greatest Name of Allah (*ism Allah al-a'zam*). He said: "O Abu Hurayrah, keep to the last verses of Surah al-Hashr and recite them often." I repeated my question to him and he repeated his answer to me; I repeated it again and he repeated it to me again.

Jabir ibn Zayd said: The Greatest Name of Allah is indeed "Allah," because of the position of this verse.

It is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Hashr, Allah will forgive him what he has done before and what he has done after."

It is narrated from Abu Umamah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the final verses of Surah al-Hashr by night or by day, and Allah takes him in that night or on that day, Allah has indeed made Paradise obligatory for him."
